title: Autoscaling Decision Engine: throughput targets, algorithmic strategies, and guardrails
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a production-ready autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated capacity that selects target metrics (throughput, latency, GPU util, queue depth), runs scaling algorithms (reactive step-scaling, PID controller, simple predictive smoothing), and enforces safety limits (scale rate caps, min/max fleet size, prewarm budgets, cost ceilings). The engine should be pluggable (policy templates per customer), simulatable against historical workloads, observable (Grafana dashboards and per-decision traces), and support gradual rollout with canary and A/B policy comparisons.
background: Customers on Dedicated frequently request predictable throughput guarantees while keeping costs bounded. Current ad-hoc autoscalers either oscillate under bursty LLM traffic or scale too slowly for short-lived spikes. We need a deterministic decision engine that balances latency SLOs, throughput commitments, and cost guardrails. Work ties to Dedicated service-level capabilities and Console rollout controls.
design_decisions: Primary target metrics: 1) 95th-percentile token-serving latency (p95_latency_ms), 2) effective throughput (tokens/s or requests/s adjusted for model length), 3) GPU utilization (avg over 30s window), 4) queue_depth (pending requests)

Scaling algorithms: provide three built-in modes - (A) reactive step-scaling based on threshold crossings, (B) PID controller tuned for steady-state throughput, (C) predictive exponential smoothing forecast for traffic slope and preemptive scale-ups. Customers can pick or we auto-select based on model/traffic profile.

Safety limits: configurable max_scale_per_minute (default 2x/min), min_replicas and max_replicas bound per pool, prewarm_budget fraction (default 0.10), cost_cap as soft alert and hard stop, cooldown window after scale events, and mandatory validation that new replica types match compatible model variants.

Decision frequency: default 15s evaluation tick with 30s smoothing windows to avoid reacting to microbursts. Offer a low-latency mode (5s ticks) for customers with strict SLOs but require higher prewarm budgets.
Fallback: if metric telemetry fails or is delayed >60s fall back to conservative scaling policy (min replicas + small step up) and route to hosted fallback model if configured.
Safety-first rollout: enable canary policy deploys to 10% of traffic for 2 hours with metrics comparison and automatic rollback on regressions in p95 latency or error rate.

Observability: Emit per-decision trace containing input metrics, chosen algorithm, proposed_delta, resulting desired_replicas, and rationale string. These traces feed into Console rollout and cost dashboards.
Simulation: provide offline simulator that replays historical traces from metrics store and calculates hypothetical cost, latency, and scale events for a candidate policy configuration.
Compatibility: policy engine implemented as part of runtime orchestration layer; pluggable adapters for Kubernetes, internal pool manager, and on-prem orchestrators.

Trade-offs: predictive mode reduces missed latency SLOs on ramp-ups but increases cold-start cost; PID is stable for steady traffic but less responsive to step changes; step-scaling is simplest to reason about but can oscillate without proper cooldowns and hysteresis. We will surface expected trade-offs in Console recommendations.
Security: policy decisions do not include customer prompt content. Telemetry uses aggregated metrics only. Config changes require RBAC with audit logs (covered in Private deployment workstream).
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports at least three built-in algorithms (step, PID, predictive) selectable per pool
Decision traces emitted for every evaluation tick and visible in Console rollout traces
Simulator available to replay 7-day historical traces and produce cost/latency comparison report
Default safety limits enforced: max_scale_per_minute, prewarm_budget, min/max replicas—configurable via API
Canary rollout mechanism implemented (traffic split, metric comparison, automatic rollback)

End-to-end e2e load test shows no more than 10% p95 latency regressions vs baseline when running predictive mode for bursty traffic and no more than 2x short-term cost increase attributable to prewarms
Documentation and UX help strings in Console with recommendations and expected trade-offs

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Oscillation under highly bursty traffic -> Mitigation: cooldown windows, hysteresis thresholds, and step caps
Risk: Cost blowup from predictive prewarms -> Mitigation: per-customer cost_cap soft+hard enforcement and post-deploy budget alerts
Risk: Metric blackout causes bad decisions -> Mitigation: fallback conservative policy and health-check gating
Risk: Incorrect tuning for specific model families -> Mitigation: provide per-model/default profiles and run auto-tuning jobs during onboarding
